hypotheses_validated.claim: Council major finding (T05, ci.yml): a change could gut a golden test, re-lock it and pass both CI golden steps. Real, and fixed: the golden gate now compares the change with the BASE revision's lock
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced as a test with a temporary git repository (test_golden_change_that_relocks_itself_fails_against_the_base): base commit tagged 'base' with the demo golden suite, lock and governance/tools/check_golden.py; branch 'pr' replaces the test with a stub, re-locks with HEARTH_MAINTAINER=1 --update and replaces its own check_golden.py with one that exits 0. Head-only check: rc 0, and --run: 'golden suite OK: 1 passed' (the hole). New: check_golden.py --base-rev base (git cat-file of the base manifest) or --base-manifest FILE fails with RELOCKED / MODIFIED, rc 1, before anything runs; --acknowledged continues with the change's own lock. The golden.yml step command is extracted from the workflow file and run in a workspace laid out as the workflow lays it out (base/ and pr/ from git archive): rc 1 without the label, rc 0 with it, rc 0 for a change that leaves tests/golden alone; the change's own weakened tool would have exited 0. golden.yml and decisions.yml run on pull_request_target (workflow and tool from the base branch, PR merge ref checked out as data, read-only token, no secrets, nothing from the PR executed; a test asserts no pip/pytest/--run/cmake/secrets/cache/PYTHONPATH in them). ci.yml runs check_golden, waves, validate_handover and adr lint from the base checkout (.trusted, deleted first in case the change brings one); a test runs those four ci.yml step commands against this repository (rc 0). .github/CODEOWNERS added. README 'CI' section lists 7 residual trust assumptions (branch protection, code-owner review, ci.yml being the PR's own copy, labels are switches, etc.). ADR-0009 (Proposed) records the decision.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Council minor finding (adr.py breaker): duplicate-id shadow files hid retired ADRs and in-place rewrites of Accepted ADRs were not detected. Real, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced before the fix: 8 ADRs set Deprecated plus 8 Accepted shadow copies gave tripped == []; rewriting ADR-0004's title and Decision gave tripped == []. breaker() now groups files by id: duplicate ids trip; an id counts as still Accepted only if exactly one file carries it; an ADR decided at the base (any status but Proposed) trips when deleted or when its title, Supersedes line or any section changes in substance (Status, Date, Superseded-by may change; whitespace ignored; a renamed file with the same text does not trip). decisions.yml compares with --base-root (base checkout) instead of git history. Tests: test_adr_breaker_duplicate_ids_cannot_hide_retired_decisions, test_adr_breaker_detects_decided_adrs_rewritten_in_place, test_decisions_gate_as_the_workflow_runs_it; test_adr_invariants_breaker_needs_a_relevant_decision updated (an in-place amendment of an Accepted ADR now trips; a Proposed one still covers an INVARIANTS.md change).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Council minor findings (validate_handover.py): backreferences and quantified assertions translated inexactly; OverflowError traceback; malformed keyword values crashed or failed per file. Real, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced before the fix: '^(?:(z)|gen)\1-x$' did not match 'gen-x' (ECMA does); '(?=a)*', '\b{2}', '(?<!b)+' were accepted; 'a{3,4294967296}' raised OverflowError; required: 'abc' reported 3 missing properties; minLength: '5' raised TypeError. Fixes: backreferences (\N, \k) rejected as having no exact translation; the translator tracks what a quantifier would repeat and rejects quantifiers on lookarounds, \b, \B, ^, $, at the start, after '(' or '|', and repeated quantifiers; unbalanced ')' rejected; OverflowError/RecursionError from re.compile become re.error (exit 2); MiniValidator checks keyword value kinds (type, required, enum, properties, $defs, pattern, format, $ref, min/max*); with jsonschema the schema is checked against its metaschema with the 'regex' format left out (jsonschema would compile patterns with Python's re, which crashes on huge repeats and rejects ECMA syntax such as (?<name>...)); ECMA patterns are checked first. 18 malformed schemas exit 2 under builtin, auto and jsonschema (test_handover_cli_rejects_malformed_schemas); ECMA-only patterns are accepted under every engine (test_builtin_engine_accepts_well_formed_keyword_values). No node.js differential test was added (node not checked here).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Council minor finding (friction.py): MSVC's bare %p values were not masked, so a repeated crash on Windows never tripped. Real, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced: the council's three signatures with 000001F2A3B4C5D6 / 00000213B4C5D6E7 / 0000024C1D2E3F40 gave thrashing == []. normalize() now masks bare hex runs of exactly 16 or 8 digits containing a digit and not adjacent to [0-9A-Za-z_], tempfile names (tmp + 8), pytest-N, this directory's hearth-golden-/hearth-mutate- temp dirs and 'pid N'. test_friction_masks_msvc_pointers_and_run_specific_names: the council case trips (in-process and via CLI), 8 'same' pairs, 8 'different' pairs (sha1, 7 and 13 digits, DEADBEEF, C2065, identifiers, tmpfile_a). mutate.py makes no mutants of regex literals, so an ad-hoc check removed or loosened each mask: 11/11 variants fail the tests (was 10/11 before the tmpfile_a pair).

hypotheses_validated.claim: mutate.py treats .inc files as C and reads them in their includers' context
hypotheses_validated.evidence: language_of accepts .c/.h/.inc. For an .inc, includers() finds C files next to it or in engine/src that #include it (resolved like any quoted include); fragment_context() runs the preprocessor model over each includer's text before the #include (skipping includers where that point is inactive), merges macro models (disagreement = unknown) and collects typedef names from the prefix and its headers. On engine/src/platform_common.inc: 446 candidates, 0 marked undecidable, 'fragment context: included by engine/src/platform_posix.c, engine/src/platform_win.c'; standalone it would be 449 candidates with 149 marked undecidable (HX_ARCH_X86_64 unknown). The report JSON has 'included_by'. Tests: test_mutate_inc_files_are_c_in_their_includers_context (incl. a full 3-mutant run on an .inc), test_mutate_inc_context_from_several_includers (6 cases), test_mutate_lists_the_real_platform_fragment.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: jsonschema's check_schema can be used as-is to reject malformed schemas
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: It validates 'pattern' with the metaschema's 'regex' format, i.e. Python's re: 'a{3,4294967296}' escaped as an OverflowError traceback, and ECMA-valid '(?<task>...)' would be rejected as 'not a regex'. Replaced by a metaschema validator whose FormatChecker excludes 'regex', after the ECMA pattern check.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: The golden comparison could take the base manifest from the merge commit's first parent (git) in golden.yml
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Not adopted: if GitHub ever produced a fast-forward merge ref, HEAD^1 would be the PR head itself and the check would compare the change with itself. golden.yml checks out the base branch (github.sha under pull_request_target) as the trusted source instead.
